problem: Existing VLN needs overly detailed step-by-step instructions, and ObjectNav only handles fixed object categories; neither handles natural high-level instructions that require reasoning about spatial relations among objects and areas (e.g. 'wait in the free area left of the sofa').
motivation: Real human commands express abstract intent and spatial constraints on objects and areas. Current navigation frameworks and VLMs lack spatial-aware instance localization tied to navigation, so a new task, data and method are needed to bridge perception and action.
key_idea: Decompose spatial navigation hierarchically: a general VLM extracts the goal description from the instruction, a fine-tuned pointing VLM (NaviPoint) outputs egocentric goal pixels, and a depth-built map with FMM planning (Map-to-Action) converts them to actions.
insight: The ablations indicate that both the reasoning VLM and task-specific pointing training matter: replacing NaviPoint with GPT-4o pointing lowers SR from 41.1% to 25.4%, and dropping the reasoning stage gives 12.4% SR. Map-based planning also beats PointNav (28.0% SR) and direct-and-avoid (15.0%). Note that NaviPoint is fine-tuned on in-simulator data from the same domain, and the paper reports no variance or seeds.
method: Spatial navigation task: SpON (object with spatial constraints) and SpAN (free area defined by spatial relations); success = Done within 1.0 m of goal; actions MoveAhead/RotateLeft/RotateRight/Done.

Dataset generation: AI2THOR GT semantics give (object, relation, reference) triplets from 50K observations (left/right/above/below/near/next to). GPT-4 writes instructions, and A* generates 10-30-step expert trajectories; 10K trajectories (5K SpON, 5K SpAN).
Reasoning VLM: GPT-4o (frozen) parses the high-level instruction into a goal description, e.g. 'the open space on the left side of the sofa'.

NaviPoint: Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-tuned with SFT (cross-entropy) on 200K spatial-relation QA pairs (100K object, 100K region) from 200 AI2THOR scenes, outputting text point coordinates in the egocentric RGB image.
Map construction: a 480x480 multi-channel map (obstacle, explored, free; 5 cm cells) is built incrementally from RGB-D and pose.

Map-to-Action: transforms the egocentric goal pixel to global map coordinates via pose and depth, plans with FMM, converts waypoints to discrete actions (turn if |angle| > 15°), and replans with new obstacles.

setting.training_data: 200K spatial-relation QA pairs (100K object, 100K region goals) from 200 AI2THOR indoor scenes; the navigation dataset has 10K trajectories
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead / RotateLeft / RotateRight / Done (via FMM waypoints, 15° turn threshold)
setting.privileged: agent pose from the simulator (GT pose/odometry); GT semantics used only for dataset generation, not at test

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,315 trajectories in unseen AI2THOR scenes (713 SpON, 602 SpAN)

numbers_note: Benchmark is the paper's own new AI2THOR spatial navigation set (not a canonical benchmark). Many ablation tables were also reported; only key variants are listed. Some ablation numbers look internally inconsistent (e.g. Table 3 GPT-4o pointing row NE 2.89 equals Table 2 Qwen2.5-VL-7B reasoning row), so interpret carefully.
results: SpNav reaches 41.1% SR / 34.8 SPL / 1.10 NE on the averaged benchmark, versus the strongest navigation-specific baseline MapNav (21.1% SR, 32.1 SPL, 2.54 NE) and the best closed-source VLM Claude-3.5-Sonnet (5.4% SR). Open-source general VLMs score 0% SR. It also transfers qualitatively to real-world scenes without additional training.
limitations: Evaluated only on the authors' own AI2THOR benchmark using simulator pose; real-world results are only qualitative with no quantitative numbers
Depends on GPT-4o for instruction reasoning and on GT-annotated synthetic data; baselines are adapted by prompt only and are not trained on the new dataset, which may make the comparison unfair
Tasks assume the goal is visible in the current egocentric view ('what you see is what you reach') and have no exploration component
